chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Stoning does not become obligatory until the proof is established by four witnesses that they have indeed seen him having intercourse with her.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ: the number four, indicating the required count of witnesses
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: the legally valid proof or evidentiary establishment
key_terms.شُهُودٍ: witnesses who testify to the act

ai.seo_question: When does stoning become legally established in a zina case according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that the hadd of rajm is not to be carried out unless the required proof is established through four witnesses. It emphasizes the strict evidentiary standard in cases of zina and the seriousness of judicial procedure in Islamic law.
